_about: The board library for brain/workshop.py. Every new workshop holds every board below, in this order; `on` says which arrive switched on. Content here is the default a new deck starts with; a deck keeps its own copy, so editing this file never changes a workshop that already exists. Keys are permanent: a deck stores each board's answers under its key.

boards.name: Opening
boards.title: From first sight to the most important task

questions.q: What should a customer feel?
questions.d: From first seeing the brand to finishing their most important task in the product.

questions.q: What should they understand?
What should they be able to do?

boards.name: Team
boards.title: Who you’ll work with
boards.about: Names and roles on both sides; RACI and next steps pick owners from here.

questions.q: Why is this happening now, and what is not working today?
What should it drive?
questions.d: Signups, retention, conversion, trust, pricing power, expansion.

questions.q: What does success look like at launch, in three months, in a year?
What must stay unchanged?
questions.d: Name, logo, core colours, the product promise, legal claims, what customers expect.

questions.q: What evidence do we have?
questions.d: Analytics, support tickets, interviews, sales objections, churn reasons.

boards.name: Mission and positioning
boards.title: Why this exists
boards.about: Vision, mission, positioning, difference and the one idea, in the client’s words.

rows.label: Vision
rows.def: The world if this fully works.

rows.label: Mission
rows.def: What the company does every day to get there.

rows.label: Positioning
rows.def: Who it is for, and what it is the best at.

rows.label: Difference
rows.def: What only this company can say.

boards.name: Goals and metrics
boards.title: What this has to achieve
boards.about: Goals, how we will measure them, and the one number that matters.

buckets.d: How we will know it worked
The one number that matters most

boards.name: Timeline
boards.about: Phases as bars and milestones as diamonds, week by week from the kickoff.

boards.name: Audiences
boards.title: Who this is for
boards.about: A profile per audience, anti-audiences too: nine questions in three groups.

questions.q: Who are they?
What are they trying to get done?
questions.prompt: The task that brings them to us, in their words.

questions.q: What frustrates them today?
questions.prompt: With what they use now, or with us.

questions.q: What do they need from us?
questions.prompt:
What would make this worth their time?
What must it do for them?

questions.q: What convinces them?
questions.prompt:
Proof, people, numbers, a feeling.
What tips them over?

questions.q: Who do they trust?
Where do they first meet us?
questions.prompt: App store, social, a referral, a sales call, search, the website.

questions.q: On what, and how confident are they?
questions.prompt: Devices, surroundings, language, accessibility needs, digital confidence.

questions.q: After the first visit, what should they think, feel and do?
Five words for the brand today, and five for where it is going
If the brand were a person, how would it speak and make decisions?
What should people feel?
questions.d: Confidence, calm, delight, urgency, authority, play.

questions.q: What is non-negotiable, and what is open to reinvention?
How should it differ from competitors, in tone and behaviour as well as looks?

boards.name: Personality
boards.title: Where should it sit?
boards.about: Eight pairs of words; drag each dot toward the word that fits.

questions.q: Are we evolving an identity or starting from nothing?

options: Refresh it and keep the core

questions.q: What can we reuse?
questions.d: Guidelines, fonts, imagery, illustration, photography, icons.

questions.q: Which references do you admire, and exactly why?
questions.d: Colour, type, density, motion, photography, layout, personality.

questions.q: Which references should we avoid, and why?
Where must the system work?
questions.d: Marketing, product UI, sales decks, social, packaging, events, future sub-brands.

questions.q: Who do customers compare you to, directly and indirectly?
What do they do well that we should match?
Where do they all look and sound the same, so we can differ?
Who must we never be mistaken for?
Which surfaces are in scope?
questions.d: Marketing site, onboarding, dashboard, checkout, settings, emails, empty states, errors.

questions.q: Which flows matter for launch, and which can wait?
Is this a redesign, a new product, or a system extension?

options: An extension of an existing system

questions.q: What content, data and imagery will we have while designing?
Languages, dark mode, breakpoints, accessibility?
Which three tasks must take the least effort?
Where do people drop off, get lost or call support today?
How simple, and how deep for power users?
Where is it worth breaking the category’s conventions?
What should motion and feedback help people understand?
Which platforms, frameworks, CMS and component libraries are in use?
Which browsers, devices and performance limits apply?
Who builds the UI, and how closely must designs match what they can build?
Which legal, privacy or industry rules affect the design?
Who keeps the content up to date after launch?
What deliverables, in what formats, by when?
What is out of scope?
What is the budget range, and what trade-offs does it imply?
Which dates are fixed, and which milestones can move?
How many review rounds, and what feedback format works best?

boards.name: Who decides
boards.title: Who decides what
boards.about: Roles against Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed; people tap in from Team.

boards.name: Ways of working
boards.about: A week, or two, of the rituals: reviews, check-ins, feedback rounds.

boards.name: Premortem
boards.title: It’s six months from now and this failed. Why?

questions.q: What would make us call this unsuccessful?
Why did it fail?
How do we prevent it?

boards.name: Next steps
boards.title: Who does what next
boards.about: Each step with an owner picked from the team.
items: Share the brand assets: logos, fonts, guidelines.
Send the list of existing pages and products.

_sources: Questions adapted from the owner's design-brief list (2026-11-06), which drew on asana.com/resources/design-brief, jvds.cn's UI design brief template and Black Country Chamber's six questions behind every design brief.
